title: A Wreck for the Current
premise: Gideon Nystrom, a disgraced mountain guide hiding in the border town of Kestrel's Landing, is handed a dying prospector's map to the source of the Vane River—a valley the mining consortium has sealed off with bribes and violence. Bound by a promise made over a corpse, Gideon and river-pilot Sera Okonkwo fight their way upstream through rapids, sabotage, and the consortium's hired hunters, discovering that the 'forbidden' source hides not gold but water rights that could break the region's power monopoly. When Gideon learns his own blacklisting was engineered years ago by the consortium's founder—his estranged father—he must choose between exposing the truth and keeping the anonymity he built his life on. In the end they reach the source as the dry season peaks, broadcast the evidence downstream, and Gideon trades invisibility for a name he can finally claim.
about_author: Coral Thackeray is the pen name of a former expedition cook who spent a decade on commercial river runs before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction draws on real route notes, drowned maps, and the stubborn people who live where roads give up.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Gideon Nystrom's POV. Working under an alias in Kestrel's Landing, Gideon takes low-paying trail jobs and avoids the registry office where his blacklisted name would surface. The beat is wary routine—the practiced choreography of a man staying invisible.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Landing
chapters.summary: Sera Okonkwo's POV. River pilot Sera watches a half-dead prospector stagger off a freight barge and into Gideon's path. She notices how gently Gideon handles the man despite his cold reputation. The beat is curiosity kindling toward someone she assumes is just another drifter.

chapters.title: The Dying Trade
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The prospector, Halloway, offers Gideon a hand-drawn map to the Vane's source in exchange for one promise: carry it upstream before the dry season ends. Gideon refuses, then finds Halloway dead at dawn. The beat is guilt arriving ahead of consent.

chapters.title: What the Map Costs
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Consortium men tear through the landing searching for Halloway's effects; Sera realizes Gideon has them and covers for him without knowing why. The beat is complicity chosen in a heartbeat.

chapters.title: Blacklisted Twice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Flashback to the avalanche on the Corren Pass that got Gideon blamed for nine deaths and banned from two countries. The chapter reveals the official story never matched what Gideon saw. The beat is old injustice reopened.

chapters.title: Terms Upstream
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Gideon asks Sera to run him up the Vane past the checkpoint weirs. She names an outrageous price; he pays it. The beat is two liars striking a bargain neither fully trusts.

chapters.title: The First Weir
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They bluff past the first consortium checkpoint using forged salvage permits. A guard studies Gideon's face too long. The beat is tension stretched thin, released too soon.

chapters.title: Rapids Called the Grinder
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. A brutal rapid nearly swamps the boat; Gideon's mountaineering rope-work saves the cargo. Sera begins revising her estimate of her passenger. The beat is grudging respect earned in white water.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Bank
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They spot consortium trackers paralleling them on shore—someone tipped off the checkpoints. The beat is the hunt becoming real, the river no longer neutral ground.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on Maps
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They shelter with a river community that survives by being unrecorded. An elder recognizes something in Gideon's surname and says nothing. The beat is warmth shadowed by recognition.

chapters.title: Halloway's Second Map
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Hidden stitching in Halloway's jacket reveals a second document: survey data proving the source feeds aquifers three provinces depend on. The beat is the promise deepening from personal debt to public stakes.

chapters.title: Sabotage at Night
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Someone slashes their fuel line at anchor. Sera catches a glimpse of a tracker's tattoo—consortium brand. The beat is paranoia taking root aboard.

chapters.title: Portage of Bones
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A grueling portage around an unrunnable gorge, hauling the boat over scree. Old injuries flare; Gideon confesses nothing but Sera sees everything. The beat is endurance as intimacy.

chapters.title: The Founder's Face
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. At a trading post, a consortium poster offers reward for 'the Nystrom boy.' Sera confronts Gideon with it. The beat is trust cracking under a hidden identity revealed.

chapters.title: Corren Pass, Retold
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon finally tells the truth: the avalanche was triggered by an unsanctioned consortium blast, covered up by his own father, Aldous Nystrom, who sacrificed his son's name to bury the evidence. The beat is confession met with silence, then belief.

chapters.title: Running the Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. A fortified weir blocks the middle river; Sera runs it at night in flood stage rather than surrender the boat. The beat is reckless courage vindicated by inches.

chapters.title: What Duty Looks Like
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Resting in a cave, Gideon admits the promise to Halloway has become something larger—and that finishing it means ending the anonymity that kept him safe. The beat is love against duty, duty winning for now.

chapters.title: The Tracker's Mercy
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The lead hunter, Vess, corners them but lets them go after reading Halloway's survey data—her own village's wells are failing. The beat is an enemy revealed as another captive of the system.

chapters.title: Dry Season Closing
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Water levels drop; the upper river will be unnavigable within days. They calculate a route that should be impossible. The beat is the clock becoming the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Split Channel
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The map and the river disagree; Sera must choose a channel on instinct alone. Her choice proves right but strands their spare supplies. The beat is expertise humbled and trusted anyway.

chapters.title: Voices in the Canyon
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Consortium loudspeakers echo through the gorge offering amnesty for the map. Gideon records the offer as evidence of what they're hiding. The beat is defiance sharpened into strategy.

chapters.title: Vess Closes In
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Vess, pressured by her handlers, resumes the hunt with a gunboat. A running chase through narrows ends with both vessels damaged. The beat is pursuit turned mutual ruin.

chapters.title: Stranded Together
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Forced ashore beside the wrecked gunboat, Gideon and Vess negotiate an uneasy truce while Sera patches the hull. The beat is enemies discovering shared ground.

chapters.title: Aldous on the Radio
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Aldous Nystrom himself broadcasts upstream, addressing 'Gideon' by name and offering full reinstatement—for the map and silence. The beat is temptation delivered in a father's voice.

chapters.title: The Offer Refused
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon answers the radio: he'll trade the truth, not for it. Aldous threatens to burn the valley's villages as 'quarantine measures.' The beat is rage transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Warning Downstream
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They divert to warn the unrecorded village; evacuation begins under smoke on the horizon. The elder who recognized Gideon's name gives him a blessing and a warning about the source. The beat is cost made concrete.

chapters.title: The Last Rapid
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The final gorge, nearly dry, must be run as a cascade of knife rocks. Sera threads it with Gideon hauling lines from the banks. The beat is mastery and terror fused.

chapters.title: Foot of the Source
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They abandon the boat and climb toward the headwaters on foot, Vess following as reluctant ally. The beat is the journey's shape changing from escape to arrival.

chapters.title: The Sealed Valley
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The source valley: springs fenced, gauging stations manned, the 'forbidden zone' revealed as a privatized watershed. The beat is awe curdling into clarity.

chapters.title: Father at the Headwaters
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Aldous arrives by helicopter with guards—not to arrest them but to plead, privately, for Gideon to come home and let the system stand. The beat is the personal climax: love weaponized as inheritance.

chapters.title: Two Maps, One Truth
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon lays Halloway's survey beside the consortium's falsified filings and sees the whole architecture of the cover-up, including Corren Pass. The beat is understanding completing itself.

chapters.title: The Choice of Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Aldous offers everything—pardon, partnership, his mother's ring—in exchange for walking away. Gideon chooses the promise instead. The beat is identity claimed over comfort.

chapters.title: Broadcast from the Source
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Using the gauging station's transmitter, they send Halloway's data to every settlement radio downstream, with Gideon speaking under his true name. The beat is courage spent all at once.

chapters.title: Guards Turned Witnesses
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The station's own technicians, hearing the broadcast, refuse orders to destroy the equipment. Vess formally logs her testimony. The beat is power's machinery refusing its master.

chapters.title: Aldous Unraveling
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Aldous orders a seizure, then watches his men stand down; his authority dissolves in the valley it was built to hide. He leaves without arresting anyone. The beat is corruption collapsing inward.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The three travel downstream together as word spreads ahead of them; checkpoints open unasked. The beat is the river, once hostile, carrying them home.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Landing Remembers
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Back at the landing, crowds and officials await; Gideon testifies plainly, asking nothing for himself except Halloway's grave marked with his real name. The beat is reckoning without triumphalism.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Investigations begin; Gideon declines reinstatement offers and instead certifies Sera's new guiding outfit on the Vane. The beat is quiet rebuilding after the fall.

chapters.title: A Wreck for the Current
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon and Sera's POVs. They launch a rebuilt boat at dawn, leaving Halloway's original map framed at the landing's ferry house. Gideon signs the register with his own name for the first time in years. The beat is peace earned, identity and love no longer at war.
